characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books & Films)
characters.summary: Théoden is the King of Rohan, fighting as a mounted knight wielding his sword Herugrim. He leads cavalry charges with inspiring leadership, though he is vulnerable to physical trauma and enemy beasts.
weaknesses: Aged physical condition compared to his prime
limitations: Limited by human stamina and the physical limits of mounted combat

sources.supports: Role as King of Rohan, use of Herugrim, leadership in battle.

feats.claim: Led the Rohirrim cavalry charge at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

notableResults.note: Théoden was crushed when his horse Snowmane fell upon him after being struck by fear and sorcery.

campaignTags.claim: Fights while riding his warhorse Snowmane in battle.

unknowns: Exact prowess in single combat prior to his old age.

characters.summary: Elu Thingol is the King of Doriath and one of the mightiest Elves of ancient days, wielding the sword Aranrúth and possessing formidable innate power and authority. He protects his realm with potent protective magic known as the girdle of Melian.

mechanisms: Protective boundary of Doriath (Girdle of Melian)

weaknesses: Prone to pride and tragic fate through the Silmarils and Dwarven disputes
mobility: Natural-flight not possessed; standard Elven foot movement
limitations: Physical form can be slain by mortal or dwarven weapons

sources.supports: King of Doriath, wielder of Aranrúth, status among the Eldar.

feats.claim: Fought and defended Beleriand alongside his people during the Elder Days.

notableResults.note: Ambushed and slain in Menegroth by rogue dwarves.

campaignTags.claim: Possesses immense power derived from his stature among the Eldar and association with Melian.

unknowns: Exact limits of his personal combat magic outside of his royal authority.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit / The Lord of the Rings
characters.summary: Thranduil is the Elvenking of Mirkwood, fighting with an elven blade and bow while mounted or on foot. He possesses typical high-end Elven agility, martial skill, and centuries of combat experience.
weaknesses: Prone to isolationism and emotional detachment regarding outsiders
limitations: Mortal if subjected to fatal wounds

sources.supports: Elvenking of Mirkwood, participation in the Battle of Five Armies.

feats.claim: Fought in the Battle of Five Armies, leading the forces of Mirkwood.

notableResults.note: Successfully defended positions during the Battle of Five Armies.

campaignTags.claim: Rides an elk into battle in cinematic adaptations.

unknowns: Extent of personal magic used in Mirkwood beyond traditional elven crafts.

characters.summary: Treebeard (Fangorn) is the oldest of the Ents, possessing immense tree-like strength capable of tearing apart stone walls and fortifications with his bare hands. He is slow to anger but devastating in destructive force when provoked.

mechanisms: Massive woody bark hide resistant to ordinary cuts

weaknesses: Vulnerable to fire and severe burning
limitations: Slow movement speed in ordinary conditions

sources.supports: Treebeard's identity as oldest Ent, physical strength, and attack on Isengard.

feats.claim: Led the Ents in the destruction and flooding of Isengard, tearing down stone barriers.

notableResults.note: Overwhelmed Isengard defenses effortlessly due to surprise and immense physical strength.

campaignTags.claim: Stands around fourteen feet tall as a tree-like giant.

unknowns: Exact upper limit of strength against powerful magical combatants.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit / The Lord of the Rings
characters.summary: Troll Chieftains are massive, brutal brutes possessing immense physical strength and wielding heavy clubs or war hammers. They rely on sheer blunt-force trauma to crush opponents.

mechanisms: Thick hide and heavy muscle mass

weaknesses: Turned to stone by direct sunlight (in standard Tolkien lore)
Low intelligence and susceptibility to trickery
limitations: Inability to operate during daylight hours without turning to stone (unless specifically Olog-hai variants)

sources.supports: Characteristics, physical strength, and weakness to sunlight for standard trolls.

feats.claim: Crushed numerous combatants in melee combat during major skirmishes.
feats.citation: The Lord of the Rings / The Hobbit

campaignTags.claim: Enormous creatures standing well over ten feet tall.

unknowns: Individual name distinctions for generic Troll Chieftains.
